title: Git Undo & Recovery: Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on undoing work in Git: restore, reset modes, revert, amend, reflog recovery, restoring deleted branches and safely undoing pushed commits.

chapters.title: Undo Mental Model: Three Areas
points: Three areas: working tree, index (staging), and repository (HEAD commit); every undo command targets one or more of them
Local unpublished history can be rewritten; published (pushed, shared) history should only be undone by adding new commits
Before any undo, run `git status` and `git log --oneline -5` to see which area holds the change
Committed work is rarely truly lost: commits stay reachable via reflog for ~90 days (unreachable ~30 days) until gc prunes them
Uncommitted changes are the only truly unrecoverable loss: `git restore` and `reset --hard` on never-committed edits cannot be undone

chapters.title: Restore and Unstage Files
points: `git restore <file>` discards working-tree edits by copying from the index (destructive, no undo)
`git restore --staged <file>` unstages a file but keeps the edits in the working tree
`git restore --source=<commit> <file>` pulls a file's version from any commit; add `--staged --worktree` to update both
`git restore -p` interactively discards chosen hunks only
`git checkout -- <file>` and `git reset HEAD <file>` are the older equivalents of restore

chapters.title: Reset: Soft, Mixed, Hard
points: `git reset` moves the current branch pointer to the given commit; the mode decides what else changes
`--soft`: moves HEAD only; undone changes remain staged (ideal for redoing or squashing the last commits)
`--mixed` (default): moves HEAD and resets the index; changes remain in the working tree as unstaged
`--hard`: moves HEAD, resets index and working tree; uncommitted edits are lost, so check `git status` first
Example: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` undoes the last commit and keeps the files staged; `HEAD~3` goes back three commits
`git reset --hard ORIG_HEAD` undoes a bad merge or reset, since ORIG_HEAD records the previous tip

chapters.title: Amend and Revert
points: `git commit --amend` replaces the last commit: fix its message, or stage more files and add them without a new commit
`git commit --amend --no-edit` keeps the message while adding newly staged changes
Amend creates a new commit hash, so never amend a commit that is already pushed
`git revert <commit>` creates a new commit that inverts that commit's changes and leaves history intact
`git revert -m 1 <merge-commit>` reverts a merge, where -m picks the mainline parent (1 = the branch you merged into)
`git revert A..B` reverts a range, and `--no-commit` (-n) combines several reverts into one commit

chapters.title: Reflog and Recovering Lost Work
points: `git reflog` lists where HEAD (and each branch) pointed over time, with entries like `HEAD@{2}`; it is local only and never pushed
Recover after a bad reset or rebase: find the pre-mistake entry, then `git reset --hard HEAD@{n}`
Recover a deleted branch: `git reflog`, find its last commit hash, then `git branch <name> <hash>`
`git branch -D` deletes the branch label only; the commits remain until gc, so recovery is quick
A dropped stash or dangling commit can be found with `git fsck --lost-found`, then restored with `git branch <name> <hash>`
Reflog expires: default 90 days for reachable entries and 30 days for unreachable ones, so recover promptly

chapters.title: Undoing Pushed Commits Safely: Cheat Sheet
points: Pushed to a shared branch: use `git revert <hash>` then a normal `git push`, with no force needed
If you must rewrite your own pushed branch, use `git push --force-with-lease`, never bare `--force`, because it refuses when the remote has new commits
Never reset or amend commits on main or any branch teammates have pulled
Cheat: file edit `restore <f>`; unstage `restore --staged <f>`; last commit `reset --soft HEAD~1`; discard all `reset --hard`; shared commit `revert`; lost commit `reflog` + `reset --hard HEAD@{n}`
Decision rule: local and unpushed means reset or amend; pushed and shared means revert; panicking means reflog first
